title: Multiscale competency shields mutations from selection and smooths fitness landscapes

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Multiscale competency shields mutations from selection and smooths fitness landscapes

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In organisms with a multiscale competency architecture, whose modules actively correct toward a target morphology, mutations that would be detrimental in hardwired organisms (e.g. displacing the eye) become neutral, so the architecture shields some of mutations' negative effects from selection and smooths the fitness landscape.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Evolutionary Aspects › Multi-Scale Autonomy Potentiates the Speed of Evolution

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Thus, MCA shields from selection some aspects of mutations’ negative effects (which inevitably are the bulk of random mutations’ consequences).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds”, Frontiers in systems neuroscience (2022), doi:10.3389/fnsys.2022.768201; section “Evolutionary Aspects › Multi-Scale Autonomy Potentiates the Speed of Evolution”. Scope: Evolving multicellular organisms; computational models of evolution with competent cells

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-tame-29: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.59

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The shielding and smoothing predictions have direct computational metrics and can be tested in specified models. Existing analyses address restricted architectures, leaving the broad biological prediction only partly resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In published or reimplemented evolutionary models, compare fitness effects of identical mutations with competent error-correcting modules enabled versus disabled, measuring deleterious-effect distributions and landscape ruggedness.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Comparable empirical mutation datasets are scarce.

Simulation support may not generalize to evolving organisms.

Results depend strongly on how competence and target morphology are modeled.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.58
discriminating power: 0.68
analysis feasibility: 0.62
operationalizability: 0.7
data adequacy: 0.38

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The prediction has a clear computational contrast: the same disruptive mutation should be less visible to selection when competent modules correct anatomy. That run was not located as public code or output, and organismal datasets do not contain the paired with-versus-without comparison. Resolving the claim needs that simulation or a new comparative measurement.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In an evolutionary simulation, compare the fitness effect and fixation of a morphology-displacing mutation with and without a module that corrects anatomy toward a target; shielding holds if the same mutation is more nearly neutral when correction is present.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
No deposited simulation was found that already compares fitness landscapes with and without morphogenetic correction.

Comparative mutational-robustness data for regulative versus mosaic developers are too sparse to stand in for that contrast.
